claim: TuRBO (Eriksson et al., NeurIPS 2019) is the actual literature source that explicitly discusses an optimizer 'appearing stuck' in local Bayesian optimization, handled through an explicit trust-region shrink/restart heuristic rather than any UCB/LCB sign-based argument -- making it a stronger candidate true-owner than fan2024minucb for a generic 'BO can get stuck locally' framing, though it does not describe the specific mechanism (acquisition locally maximal exactly at data) claimed in the audited paper.
stance_target: Search for the true owner of 'optimizer gets stuck / doesn't move' framing in local BO literature (task e)
quoted_support: "The typical behavior is to expand a TR when the optimizer 'makes progress', i.e., it finds better solutions in that region, and shrink it when the optimizer appears stuck. Therefore, following, e.g., Nelder and Mead [33], we will shrink a TR after too many consecutive 'failures', and expand it after many consecutive 'successes'." (Section 2, line 182-186)

claim: TuRBO uses Thompson sampling over local Gaussian processes for candidate selection, not a UCB or LCB argmin/argmax exploitation step, and never discusses distance-aware uncertainty or an offline setting -- it is only a partial match for the audited paper's mechanism, useful for the general 'stuck locally' framing but not for the specific LCB-at-data mathematics.
stance_target: Precision of TuRBO as a substitute citation for the LCB-paralysis mechanism specifically
scope_conditions: TuRBO's candidate-selection mechanism, described in main text and appendix
quoted_support: "a TR should be sufficiently large to contain good solutions. On the other hand, it should be small enough to ensure that the local model is accurate within the TR." (line 181-182)
